title: Relative profinite test objects and their normalized label maps
statement:
Use compatible universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. For a profinite space $S$ put $a(S)=\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{LC}(S,\mathbf Z)$, with $\operatorname{LC}$ the ring of locally constant integer-valued functions, and let $X[S]$ be the inverse limit of $\coprod_{S_i}X$ over finite continuous quotients $S\to S_i$, as in [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor]. There is a canonical isomorphism $X[S]\cong X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}a(S)$ natural in $X$ and $S$. Let $r_{X,S}:|X[S]|\to S$ be projection to $S$ after $|X[S]|\to|a(S)|$ and the inverse of the homeomorphism $(s,\mathfrak p)\mapsto\{h:h(s)\in\mathfrak p\}$ from $S\times\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ to $|a(S)|$ [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-prime-spectrum]. For finite $S$, this is the label of the disjoint open summand of $X[S]=\coprod_S X$. For a continuous map $v:S\to T$ one has $r_{X,T}\circ|X[v]|=v\circ r_{X,S}$. For $f:Y\to X$, the canonical identification $Y\times_X X[S]\cong Y[S]$ satisfies $r_{X,S}\circ|\operatorname{pr}_{X[S]}|=r_{Y,S}$. For every affine $X$-scheme $U$, the map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(U,X[S])\longrightarrow C(|U|,S),\qquad \phi\longmapsto r_{X,S}\circ|\phi|$$
is a bijection, natural in $S$ and affine $U$. Writing $q_U:|U|\to\pi_0(|U|)$ for the connected-component quotient, its inverse at $q_U$ is an $X$-map $\phi_U:U\to X[\pi_0(|U|)]$. If $r_{X,S}|\phi|=gq_U$, then $\phi=X[g]\phi_U$.

proof.text: Use the actual definition of profiniteToProEtOf: its scheme is the pullback a(S) x_specZ X and its structure morphism is the second projection. The pullback symmetry gives e with the required two projection identities. Define r by composing the first pullback projection with the inverse evaluation-prime homeomorphism and its first coordinate.

The proved private helper profiniteProjection_natural in ProEtalePointComponentsMaps computes the evaluation-prime label after Spec of precomposition. The first projection of the pullback map commutes with the absolute map profiniteToScheme.map v. Compose these identities to obtain naturality of r.

Put F = profiniteToProEtOf X followed by the forgetful functor to Over X. The existing proof helper coproducts_of_continuous in ProfiniteTestObjectFunctor shows that F preserves finite coproducts, since it is continuous for the coherent and pro-etale topologies. Finite-limit preservation identifies F(point) with the terminal object id_X of Over X. The point maps into a finite discrete S form a colimit cofan in Profinite, including empty S. Apply F and Over.forget X, which preserves colimits as a left adjoint, then transport the summands across F(point) isomorphic to id_X. This gives the colimit cofan j. Each j is over X by construction. Evaluation at the unique point is an explicit ring isomorphism LC(point,Z) isomorphic to ULift Z. Its spectrum identifies the absolute projection of F(point) with the structure map of X followed by its inverse. Composing with the absolute image of the point map computes the projection of j_s as Spec of evaluation at s. Label naturality for point -> S shows that j_s has constant label s.

The pullback symmetry, pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso, and the terminal identity f then toSpecZ X = toSpecZ Y give the canonical base-change isomorphism. Their projection identities give exactly the two displayed equations for its inverse. Composing the absolute projection equation with the evaluation-prime label proves label compatibility for arbitrary f.

For arbitrary affine U over X, the pullback universal property and terminality of Spec Z give an explicit equivalence between Hom_X(U,X[S]) and Hom(U,a(S)). Use the proved stronger private affineMapEquiv and affineMapEquiv_apply of ProEtalePointComponentsMaps. These identify Hom(U,a(S)) with C(U,S) and compute the forward map as the first coordinate under the inverse evaluation-prime homeomorphism. Consequently the composite equivalence is exactly phi -> r composed with phi, so this map is bijective. No pro-etale or weak-contractibility hypothesis on U is needed by these helpers.

Naturality in the affine source is associativity of continuous-map composition. Naturality in S follows by precomposing label naturality with phi. Surjectivity of the affine bijection for S = pi_0(U) supplies phi_U with label the quotient map. Given phi with label g composed with the quotient map, label naturality gives the same label for phi_U followed by X[g]; injectivity of the affine bijection proves the stated factorization. These arguments include empty U and empty S.
